decision: The public RPC cuts the hunter's streams and then refuses it with HTTP 413; a paid feed is out of reach. Restart the hunter now on the instrumented code with two streams, restart it on one stream, wait for a natural restart, or add a free keyed failover?

gates.from: python -m pytest, 2026-10-05, after the last change to ops/hunt.py
the operator, 2026-10-05: 'make this work on the free tier'

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: Every cut is a server-side Close with a non-RFC code; the client's 1002 is its answer, not the cause. A lenient client would not keep the stream

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: The 413 is a per-IP free-tier meter overdrawn: endpoint-remaining -19570, retry-after 30, pubsub-remaining 7 of 10 with three subscriptions open from this IP

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: Two streams: 286 cuts a day, 84 % absorbed by the twin, 343 blind seconds a day, 5.0 % of records touched

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: The patched hunter journals every both-down window to journal/gaps, logs the meter on every handshake and refusal, honours retry-after, takes IRV_FLOW_STREAMS (default 2) and no longer miscounts a live twin when the other is refused; 48 tests green

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: The operator has no funds for a paid feed

rows.label: INFERENCE
rows.text: One stream halves the IP's draw but loses the twin that absorbs 84 % of cuts: it wins only if the cut rate per connection falls by more than half, and nothing on disk says whether cuts follow the meter

rows.label: INFERENCE
rows.text: The meter read at each reconnect after a cut tells whether cuts come with the budget overdrawn; the patched hunter records exactly that, so one day on two streams answers I01 without betting the record on it

rows.label: ASSUMPTION
rows.text: A restart costs the mints watched at that moment, about 480, the same order as two hours of blind windows

rows.label: HYPOTHESIS
rows.text: The cuts are the meter: drawing half as much would cut the cut rate by more than half

rows.label: UNKNOWN
rows.text: The meter's unit and refill; whether a keyed free failover would be served at all on the free plan's websocket limits

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: THE CONSTRAINT: COLLECT — heartbeat 0 s, last event 1 s ago, drops this hour 144, streams up 2, lag 2.3 s

rows.label: INFERENCE
rows.text: [OPEN] Stop the hunter and let the scheduled guard start the patched one on two streams; journal the restart gap; for 24 h read the meter logged at every post-cut handshake. If most post-cut meters are negative, a one-stream trial is the next decision; if not, the budget is not the driver and two streams stay

rows.label: HYPOTHESIS
rows.text: [OPEN] Restart the patched hunter now with IRV_FLOW_STREAMS=1 and compare blind seconds a day against 343

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: [OPEN] Leave pid 20212 running; the patch goes live whenever the guard or a logon next starts the hunter

rows.label: HYPOTHESIS
rows.text: [VETOED] Add a third stream on the Helius free plan that connects only while both public streams are down, about 100 MB a day against 1M credits a month

rows.label: FACT
rows.text: [VETOED] Move the hunter to a paid feed

rows.label: INFERENCE
rows.text: RULED: restart the patched hunter now on two streams through the guard, journal the restart gap, and read the meter at every post-cut handshake for 24 h before touching the stream count. One stream (B) is the obvious move and the likely wrong one: the twin absorbs 84 % of cuts and H01 is contested. Waiting (C) leaves the outages unrecorded. The keyed failover (D) and a paid feed (E) are vetoed on the prereg and on funds.

vetoed.D-free-keyed-failover: rule 2: the prereg names a keyless feed; the change waits on an amendment and the operator's signup, neither of which exists
vetoed.E-paid-feed: F05: no funds; and rule 2, the prereg names the public RPC
